chunks: There was issued from Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), when al-Zubayrī—may Allah curse him—was killed: “This is the recompense of one who dared against Allah concerning His awliyā'. He claimed that he would kill me and that I would have no offspring. So how did he see the power of Allah concerning him?”
And a son was born to him, whom he named M Ḥ M D, in the year two hundred and fifty-six.

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the Imam speaking in the report
key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His awliyā', meaning Allah’s chosen guardians
key_terms.الزُّبَيْرِيُّ: al-Zubayrī, the hostile figure mentioned in the narration
key_terms.قُدْرَةَ اللَّهِ: the power of Allah as manifested in events

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah’s response to the one who claimed Imam Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) would be killed without offspring?
ai.summary: This report states that Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) declared the death of al-Zubayrī to be a recompense for his audacity against Allah in opposing His awliyā'. It also affirms the birth of the Imam’s son, presented as a manifestation of Allah’s power against the claim that the Imam would leave no offspring.
